title: Enzymes in medicine and industry; Cloning and biotechnology; Prokaryotic cells and viruses
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: CE04a#t4 term and clue written for the game; CE04a#t1 term and clue written for the game; CE04a#t2 term and clue written for the game; CE04a#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: CE04a#N.3a, EZ05#N.4, GR09a#N.3, GR09c#N.15b, CE04a#N.9, CE04a#N.13a.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Lysozyme
items.clue: An enzyme that strips away the wall of a bacterium

items.label: Prokaryotic
items.clue: Describes cells with no nucleus, such as bacteria and archaea

items.label: Nucleoid
items.clue: Region of cytoplasm where a bacterium's circular DNA lies free

items.label: Peptidoglycan
items.clue: The material of the wall outside a bacterium's plasma membrane

questions.stem: Which description of the structure of a Bacillus cell is correct?

options.text: A loop of naked DNA lies in the cytoplasm, and proteins are made on 70S ribosomes.
The DNA is enclosed by a nuclear membrane inside a small nucleus within the cytoplasm.
The cell wall outside the plasma membrane is built from long parallel fibres of cellulose.
The DNA loop is wound around histone proteins to package it within the nucleoid region.

questions.explanation: A Gram-positive eubacterium such as Bacillus has a cell wall, a plasma membrane, cytoplasm, naked DNA in a loop lying in the nucleoid region of the cytoplasm, and 70S ribosomes on which its proteins are synthesised.

questions.stem: A disease is caused by over-activity of enzyme E. Researchers design drug D, an active-site-directed inhibitor of E. Which property must D have?

options.text: It must unfold the whole of enzyme E so that the active site is destroyed.
It must bind to the substrate of E so that the substrate cannot reach the enzyme.
It must be small enough to fit the active site of every enzyme it meets.
It must have a shape and charges complementary to E's active site.

questions.explanation: Fitting E's active site lets D block the substrate, and fitting only E's keeps side effects low.

questions.stem: Lactase is mixed with sodium alginate solution. Drops of the mixture fall into calcium chloride solution and set as small beads with the enzyme inside. Which method of immobilisation is this?

options.text: Adsorption
Covalent bonding
Entrapment
Membrane separation

questions.explanation: The enzyme is trapped inside a gel bead. Lactose diffuses in; glucose and galactose diffuse out.

questions.stem: A bacterium infecting a patient is resistant to every antibiotic tried. Doctors treat the infection with a phage genetically modified to infect and kill that bacterium. Which statement explains why the phage can work?

options.text: The patient's body has become resistant to antibiotics, so a different kind of drug is needed.
The phage kills by infecting and bursting the bacterium, which does not involve antibiotic targets.
Bacteria cannot become resistant to phages, because they have never met them before.
The phage carries its own ribosomes and enzymes, so it keeps multiplying even when no bacteria are left.

questions.stem: A bacterial cell contains one circular DNA molecule and six copies of a plasmid. It divides once by binary fission. Which statement about the two daughter cells is correct?

options.text: Each has one circular DNA molecule, wound around histones, and exactly three plasmids.
Each has one copy of the circular DNA; the number of plasmids in each can differ.
Each has half of the original circular DNA molecule and three of the plasmids.
Each has its circular DNA inside a new nucleus formed after the chromosomes separate.

questions.explanation: The circular DNA is replicated once, so each daughter receives one copy. Plasmids are replicated and distributed independently, so their number varies between daughter cells.

questions.stem: An electron micrograph shows a cell about 3 µm long. It has a cell wall, a paler fibrous region of DNA not enclosed by any membrane, many small dense granules, and no membrane-bound organelles. How should the cell be classified?

options.text: As a plant cell, because a cell wall is found only around the cells of plants.
As a eukaryote, because the region containing DNA must be a nucleus, as every cell has one.
As a prokaryote, because its DNA lies in a nucleoid region and it has no membrane-bound organelles.
As a eukaryote, because prokaryotic cells are too simple to contain any ribosomes.
